card.name: Adjective before a medical condition noun
card.fires_on: The adjective word that comes just before a condition noun, most often "deep" before "vein thrombosis" in risk lists. It also fires on words like "passive" before "suicidal ideation" and "soft" before "tissue".

modes.label: Deep before vein thrombosis
modes.description: The word deep right after "increased risk of" or "stroke and", ahead of vein thrombosis.
modes.example: The Women's Health Initiative (WHI) estrogen-alone substudy reported increased risks of stroke and<< deep>> vein thrombosis (DVT)

modes.label: Other modifiers in adverse-event phrases
modes.description: A modifier that starts a two-word condition or term, such as passive, soft or Superficial.
modes.example: reported<< passive>> suicidal ideation with an estimated relative risk

card.plain: It marks the first word of a medical term when the next word is predictable, such as deep before vein thrombosis.
